_this_file: The VALUES the stack's conventions consist of. scripts/seed.sh applies them
to a clean host and refuses to overwrite a host that disagrees, and CI
asserts a running stack matches this file.
The REASONING lives in docs/library-layout.md and is not duplicated here.
Each group carries a _why saying only why the key belongs in this file at
all; the argument for the value itself is in the doc.
AUTHORED FROM THE DOC, never extracted from a host. Extracting canonises
settings nobody deliberated. A setting earns a place here by appearing in
docs/library-layout.md, or by being load-bearing for a closed decision.
Incidental settings, and settings that merely happen to be set somewhere,
do not. Keys beginning with _ are commentary and are ignored by the seed.

_why: Jellyfin's root folders must use the CONTAINER path. Pointing it at the
host path yields a silently empty library - docs/library-layout.md, Roots.
Deliberately NOT declared: TypeOptions. A library created through the API
writes an empty <TypeOptions /> where a UI-created one carries a populated
block, and issue #7 left open whether empty meant 'fetch nothing'. Measured
on Jellyfin 10.11.11 with two libraries and one fixture: identical
ProviderIds, rating, genres, images and overview on both. Empty means
'fall back to defaults at runtime', so there is nothing here to pin - and
declaring it would make the seed report a spurious difference against
every library a human created in the UI.
SaveSubtitlesWithMedia is a Jellyfin default rather than a choice,
but issue #13's subtitle pipeline depends on sidecar text subtitles
sitting beside the video, so it is pinned here to make a silent
change to that default fail a build instead of a playback.
docs/library-layout.md, Movies (Radarr). renameMovies is what makes
Radarr authoritative for the tree at all. The ' - ' before the quality
label in standardMovieFormat is load-bearing and not cosmetic: measured
on Jellyfin 10.11.11, the shipped bare space lists one film twice
instead of grouping it as two versions.
copyUsingHardlinks is load-bearing for compose.yaml's rule that every
service mounts the library at the SAME container path - hardlinks and
atomic moves on import are the whole reason that rule exists.
importExtraFiles shipped OFF and silently dropped any subtitle that
arrived alongside a release: the video moved into the library and the
.srt was left behind. docs/library-layout.md, Extra files on import.
docs/library-layout.md, Shows (Sonarr). Two divergences from the
shipped defaults: the series folder carries the year, because without
one 'The Office' has to be disambiguated against unrelated shows; and
the season folder is zero-padded, because 'Season 1' sorts wrongly past
nine seasons.
The same two reasons as Radarr's, which apply to Sonarr unchanged - a
TV release carrying its own .srt drops it on import exactly as a movie
release did. Recorded here because authoring from the doc generalises
the doc's reasoning; the doc observed it on Radarr only because that is
where it was first hit.
